analysis.title: The State of AI Financing: Hyperscalers Are Back
key_insights: Hyperscalers priced about $67bn of unsecured IG bonds across US and EUR markets between October 29 and November 4. MS says this shows credit markets remain open and can absorb large supply even amid volatility.
MS expects little, if any, additional unsecured hyperscaler issuance through year-end. Reasons are elevated cash balances and alternative funding such as chip financing and secured facilities.

AI and data center debt supply is $646bn YTD across global credit markets, about 3x FY25 ($216bn). Hyperscaler total is $321bn YTD vs $93bn in the prior-year period. 4Q supply has exceeded MS expectations, driven mostly by MSFT.

MS equity colleagues keep 2027 capex forecasts unchanged after the US midterms at about $1.66tr cash capex (+75% vs 2026) and about $1.77tr in 2028. About 5 GW of US IT capacity shifts from 2028 to 2029, tied to projects in Texas and Ohio not yet under construction.

MS's Powering AI model now projects a 44 GW net US power shortfall through 2028, up from 38 GW. That equals 38% of modeled data-center power demand. The delay raises the scarcity value of existing power-secured capacity.

MS sees growing dispersion in AI credit. Risk-reward for high-quality (HQ) hyperscalers is improving as they trade near YTD wides at levels consistent with A/BBB ratings. Data center construction bonds and neoclouds are expected to see more spread volatility from construction and funding risk.

AI-related leveraged finance supply was only $5bn in October (the Volta term loan, GPU plus data center). MS expects limited supply through year-end because of higher Treasury yields, policy changes and neocloud funding concerns. HY AI-related supply had no new issue in October or early November after $13bn in September.

Data center ABS spreads widened sharply in October on three mastertrust deals totaling about $2bn. Prints include an all-time widest AAA at 200bp, the widest A/A- since mid-2023 at 325bp, and the widest BBB/BBB- since fall 2023 at 375bp on a 1.5y bond. MS attributes this to structure and anticipated supply rather than a change in view on AI.

MS expects issuers to move to low-LTV, short-duration ABS in the near term. Over the longer run it thinks demand returns only if structures partly or fully amortize. Obstacles include leases struck in a different funding environment, DSCR triggers around 1.35, and about $45bn of outstanding paper that could sit in orphaned trusts.

Chip financing is accelerating, with $103bn announced in October and $138bn YTD. MS expects chip financing via SPVs to be a meaningful part of AI-related supply over the next twelve months. Shorter terms (within 5 years) should flatten curves further.

Hyperscalers disclose $1.3tr of future lease payments for leases not yet started. MS forecasts $195bn of data center shells acquired under leases in 2027. Hyperscaler, NVDA and AVGO off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees total about $4tr.
AI-related debt is 7.4% of the IG index. Hyperscaler index debt totals $498bn (4.8% of the IG index), and 'AI enabling' semis add $87bn. AI is a much larger share of equities than of credit.

META's EUR deal drew the largest order book ever for a EUR corporate bond, EUR62.1bn on a EUR9bn deal (6.9x covered). Hyperscaler non-USD issuance is $89bn YTD, about 28% of hyperscaler volume, and recent deals have shorter maturities with no 20y+ bonds in the latest AMZN sterling and GOOGL EUR deals.

Spreads are mixed by cohort. HQ hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT) are 9bp wider than the IG index. The lower-quality group (ORCL, SPCX) is 116bp wider YTD vs 13bp for the IG index. ORCL's November new issues have widened since pricing. MSFT, META and GOOGL new issues have tightened.

ORCL held an Analyst Day, then priced a $10bn bond and $10bn equity raise. It reaffirmed its IG commitment and about $20bn of remaining FY27 funding needs, split evenly between debt and equity. MS removed the 30Y from its recommended ORCL trade because of likely limited long-end issuance. MS flags vendor financing, leverage including leases, and transparency as open questions.

Supplier and vendor financing is drawing investor scrutiny. AMZN disclosed a secured supplier-financing facility of up to $80bn. DELL's DFS-related debt exceeded $20bn last quarter vs an implied core of about $14bn, and MS sees near-term DELL spread pressure as warranted ahead of its next print.

HY data center bonds are under pressure. BB data center bonds trade about 275bp back from the BB index. CRWV unsecured debt reached CCC-like levels in October, with spreads around 1,100-1,160bp and the equity down about 49% over one month.

Neoclouds face higher funding costs and greater reliance on external capital. MS sees competition from GPU financing backed by higher-quality counterparties and tighter scrutiny of shell construction as risks to their access to capital and data center capacity.

market_movers.rationale: MS credit keeps a Buy 5Y CDS trade (entry +57bp, now +307bp) and a Sell on the ORCL 5.2% 9/26/35 bond (entry +167bp, now +300bp). It cites cash funding needs and rising lease liabilities, and removed the 30Y from its recommended trade expression.

MS sees near-term spread pressure as warranted pending clarity on its finance arm's role in AI server financing. DFS-related debt exceeded $20bn and receivables were higher last quarter, with a print later this month.
Disclosures on bespoke chip financing at its upcoming FY3Q27 print are highly anticipated by credit investors.
Unsecured bonds reached CCC levels in October (about 1,156bp spread on the 2030s). Neocloud funding concerns are weighing on supply.

sector_views.rationale: Well capitalized, with cash-to-debt of 118% and gross leverage of 1.2x. They trade at A/BBB-consistent levels, near YTD wides, and risk-reward is described as 'as good as its been all year'.

sector_views.sector: Neocloud and HY data center credit
sector_views.rationale: Exposed to construction risk, funding challenges and higher borrowing costs, with spreads widening sharply.
Spreads are at wides on structure and supply technicals. Demand likely returns only with amortizing structures.

earnings_insights: NVDA FY3Q27 print is upcoming, with credit investors expecting disclosure on bespoke chip financing. No EPS or revenue figures are given.
DELL reports again later this month. Last quarter's DFS-related debt was above $20bn, higher receivables were reported, and MS flags these as the focus.
ORCL Analyst Day outlined about $20bn of remaining FY27 funding needs, split evenly between debt and equity. It was followed by a $10bn bond and $10bn equity raise.
CIFR management said on its 3Q26 earnings call that about 51 MW is ready for service, previously expected in 1Q27. Nebius disclosed a new $3.5bn senior secured facility.
AMZN's 10-Q for the quarter ended 9/30/26 disclosed a supplier-financing arrangement including a secured loan facility of up to $80bn.

crypto_views: Bitcoin miner-turned-AI-hosting names (CIFR, WULF, GLXY, APLD) are tracked via HY data center bonds and equities. Equities are down 24-58% over one month and bonds are wider after the AI sell-off.

trade_ideas.rationale: Credit profile deterioration from cash funding needs and increasing lease liabilities tied to new data centers.
trade_ideas.risk: Constructive updates on RPO/growth and financing clarity; term loans may not play a large funding role; CDS technicals such as basis selling and construction loan hedge unwinds.

trade_ideas.rationale: Credit profile deterioration from cash funding needs and increasing lease liabilities, with large media/cable structures as relative-value comps.
trade_ideas.risk: Additional visibility on long-term monetization and delevering beyond FY28; issuance cadence may differ from assumptions.

risk_factors: Construction delays and permitting risk after the midterms, especially in Texas and Ohio.
Higher Treasury yields and borrowing costs weigh on data center and neocloud financing.
Neocloud access to credit markets, plus refinancing risk and orphaned-trust risk for data center ABS.
Peak negative FCF for hyperscalers in 2027 may require more funding transactions.
Off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments, with vendor financing that could prime unsecured creditors.
Opaque chip and supplier financing, difficult to track given confidentiality and thresholds.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 compares data center spreads across IG, HY and ABS AAA/A/BBB tiers against YTD tights, averages, wides and spot, and the text states spreads are near YTD wides for all data center-backed paper.
Exhibit 29 shows YTD spread change: LQ hyperscalers +116bp, NVDA+AVGO +54bp, HQ hyperscalers +40bp, Tech +36bp, Semis +31bp, IG +13bp.
Exhibit 66 plots CRWV unsecured spreads against the CCC index, and the caption says CRWV's unsecured debt reached CCC levels in October.
vol_and_positioning: Hyperscaler CDS: the AI basket trades about 85bp wider to CDX IG. MSFT 5Y CDS is the only one still tighter than CDX IG.
IG data center bonds trade about 150bp wide to the BBB index. BB data center bonds trade about 275bp back from the BB index.
Secondary SASB data center floater BBB/BBB- spreads widened about 100bp on the month vs 10-25bp for other property types. Data center floater AAA is about 195bp, at its widest of the year.
AI-related debt is 7.4% of the IG index and 4% of the HY index.
geopolitical: US midterm election results and newly elected governors may affect data center permitting, power access and approvals, with Texas and Ohio projects not yet under construction delayed.
Regional restrictions after the midterms could shift where investment occurs without eliminating the incentive to spend.

tension_points.bull_case: HQ hyperscalers are well capitalized (cash-to-debt 118%, gross leverage 1.2x) and trade at A/BBB-consistent levels near YTD wides. Record order books (META EUR 6.9x) show demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Off-balance-sheet leases ($1.3tr not yet started), purchase commitments, rising equity issuance and peak negative FCF in 2027 raise funding needs. HQ hyperscalers trade 9bp wider than the IG index and ORCL new issues have widened.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further construction and power delays that cut monetization, or another widening wave in the lower-quality cohort (ORCL, SPCX) spreading to HQ names.

tension_points.bull_case: Weakness is technical rather than fundamental. Capex and financing needs are growing, and an amortizing structure could bring meaningful spread tightening from AAA at 200bp.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is approaching saturation for the current soft-bullet mastertrust structure. Leases struck six months ago may be underwater, and about $45bn of paper could sit in orphaned trusts.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If ABS issuers do not introduce amortization or delevering structures, demand will not pick back up and spreads stay wide.
